Agent Memory

You might say

Will the Agent remember what I told it after I start a new conversation?

A mechanism for an Agent to save and retrieve selected information in later interactions; its scope depends on the product and settings·While coding, you want the Agent to avoid automatically editing shared components. The same conversation may retain chat history; a new one sees the preference only if project rules are read or a supported memory is saved and retrieved. Check what the new conversation actually loaded in the target project.
Know first
Conversation History
Agent Memory
Where does a shared-component rule come from in a new conversation?
Project A · original conversation
Same conversation · teaching exampleConversation resumed
Earlier instructionDo not automatically edit shared components
Available this turnThe conversation still includes it

Teaching example: the product resumed the same conversation and provided earlier messages again; retention depends on its session mechanism.

The three sources have different scopes

Conversation history: Belongs to a particular conversation. The system may provide it when that conversation resumes; retention depends on the session mechanism.

Project rules: Live in project files or settings. The Agent must actually read them in the target project for them to enter the current context.

Cross-session memory: A product may save and retrieve selected information in later interactions; there is no universal guarantee about what is saved or recalled.

Memory does not appear automatically every time

Closing a window does not mean every product deletes conversation history; a new conversation does not guarantee a preference was saved or retrieved. Check what the target conversation actually loaded.

You can say this to an AI Agent

“

This new conversation must also follow “do not automatically edit shared components.” First tell me which project rules or memories you actually loaded for this turn. If the requirement is missing, add it to this project's rules or the current request before changing code.
